subject: Mutual close plan: success anchors & verification runbook
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@novamed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation plan & mutual action items

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team here was encouraged by throughput and the prefix-caching behavior on the live run. We want to formalize a short mutual action plan that ties success criteria to acceptance tests so our procurement and security teams can sign off faster.

High level asks from our side:
- A compact pass/fail test suite for the QA sprint (3rd party health data redaction + hallucination thresholds)
- A clear cutover criterion so we can narrow the go/no-go decision to a single sprint
- Evidence we can attach to our vendor review (logs, latency histograms, SOC2 reference)

Can Redwood put together a one-sheet that maps success anchors to concrete test cases and owners? We aim to run the evaluation the week of June 7 and need the acceptance checklist by May 28 to feed procurement.

Thanks,
Lena

Subject: Re: Evaluation plan & mutual action items

Lena — appreciate the clear asks. Attached is a first draft of a Mutual Action Plan (Novamed_MAP_v1.xlsx) plus a compact verification runbook (verification-runbook.md). Key highlights:

- Success anchors (what "good" looks like):
  * Latency P95 < 180ms for 2k token median workload
  * End-to-end redaction recall >= 98% on our synthetic PHI set
  * Model hallucination false-positive rate < 2% on task-specific prompts

- Exit gates (hard blockers):
  * Failure to meet redaction recall on three consecutive smoke runs
  * Severe latency spike (>2x baseline) that cannot be mitigated by routing policies
  * Unresolved SOC2 evidence or audit log access request longer than 7 business days

- Acceptance tests (traceable):
  1) Redaction smoke test (owner: Novamed QA + Redwood CS) — script + expected metrics in eval-acceptance-tests.csv
  2) Latency load sweep (owner: Redwood infra) — server-side histograms + client-side p95 measurement
  3) Regression prompts set (owner: Novamed PM + Redwood ML) — target precision/recall per prompt group

We included an evidence matrix (what to attach to procurement) and a proposed close timeline: confirmation of MAP by May 28, test readiness week of Jun 7, final decision Jun 21.

Attachment stubs:
- Novamed_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- verification-runbook.md (markdown checklist)
- eval-acceptance-tests.csv (CSV with test vectors)

Next steps: can you and your QA lead review the acceptance tests in the CSV and flag any additions by Friday? We will run the first redaction smoke internally against a synthetic slice and share results.

Best,
Marissa

--

Subject: Re: Evaluation plan & mutual action items

Hi all — quick technical notes on the runbook and tests:

1) Redaction smoke test: we'll provide a containerized harness and a small 200-record PHI-like dataset. The harness will produce detailed logs and a per-record redaction map so you can validate recall/precision.

2) Latency load sweep: please confirm expected concurrency pattern (e.g., steady 50 rps vs bursty 200 rps). I'll precompute a P95 baseline on dedicated capacity for the 2k token median.

3) Evidence & logs: we can provide time-limited access to an audit log export and a SOC2 attestation copy. For on-request forensic traces (token-level KV cache telemetry), we'll redact any customer PII before sharing.

Note on acceptance gates: for anything that looks like intermittent flakiness, propose a "third-run confirmation" rule — if a failure is observed twice, we run a third full smoke; if it fails the third time it's an exit gate. This avoids noisy single-run failures.

Ben
